sprite_sequence.text: No, no, no -- not on the very first day!
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She feels panicked and flustered, with a burst of frustrated disbelief at already messing up on the very first day.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

sprite_sequence.text: Stupid alarm, why did you die today of all days?!
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She is flustered and panicked about being late, with a burst of irritated self-directed frustration at the alarm and a desperate need to recover control.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

sprite_sequence.text: Mom's going to say it was fate punishing me for scrolling at midnight...
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She’s flustered and self-mocking, half-panicked about being late but trying to lighten the moment with a joking complaint about her mom’s inevitable teasing.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

sprite_sequence.text: Wait, seriously? They never open this gate.
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She’s abruptly shifting from frantic panic to startled, hopeful curiosity, with a spark of relief at finding an unexpected shortcut and a lively sense that something unusual is happening.
sprite_sequence.label: surprise

sprite_sequence.text: Yeah, that was the problem, thanks.
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She’s flustered and irritated from being late, but her sharp reply also shows she’s trying to keep her pride intact and push back with embarrassed defensiveness.
sprite_sequence.label: anger

sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She feels wary and puzzled, with her earlier panic easing into cautious suspicion at the stranger’s oddly precise warning.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She feels startled and suspicious, with a flash of defensive embarrassment at being read so accurately by a stranger.
sprite_sequence.label: surprise

sprite_sequence.text: How do you know that before the board goes up?
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She is startled and uneasy, trying to sound sharp and in control while her mind races at the unsettling feeling that this girl knows far too much about her.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

sprite_sequence.text: Okay, wow. Creepy. Helpful, maybe, but creepy.
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She’s startled and uneasy, but trying to keep her composure with a nervous, half-joking edge as she processes the girl’s unsettlingly specific knowledge.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

sprite_sequence.text: Yes! I might actually make it!
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She feels a sudden burst of relieved, energized optimism, with lingering nerves turning into excited determination as she realizes she may still salvage the morning.
sprite_sequence.label: happiness

sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She is stunned and suddenly shaken, realizing the girl’s warning was real and feeling a sharp mix of fear, disbelief, and uneasy gratitude.
sprite_sequence.label: surprise

sprite_sequence.text: She said not to use the east stairs.
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: Aoi is jolted into uneasy alarm and dawning belief, her earlier nervous humor giving way to a sharp, shaken realization that the stranger’s warning may have saved her.
sprite_sequence.label: surprise

sprite_sequence.text: Oh, come on. Don't do this to me on day one.
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She feels a sharp mix of disbelief and rising panic, with her earlier annoyance turning into shaken suspicion that the strange warning was real and she’s already in over her head.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

sprite_sequence.text: Fine. School first. Panic attack later.
sprite_sequence.emotion_description: She is forcing herself into brisk, joking composure to keep moving, while underneath she feels shaken, wary, and newly convinced that something unsettling is happening.
sprite_sequence.label: fear

gpt.rationale: The sequence is mostly expressive and in-character for an outgoing girl—snappy anger, open surprise, and a bright win at 'Yes!'—but several repeated fear sprites flatten distinct beats like sarcasm, nervous laughter, and resigned self-talk.

claude.rationale: An extroverted character who 'laughs openly' and has a 'face that moves with her mood' should show far more dynamic range—yet fear dominates 8 of 14 sprites, including moments of humor, relief, and determination that demand brighter expressions; the sprite choices flatten her expressiveness into anxiety rather than capturing her outgoing, reactive nature.
